depth: In a top-down egocentric view looking down at a tiled floor (~3–5 m away, dark, and out of reach), the camera wearer's own torso and forearms at the bottom are farthest (~3–5 m, brightest white, and out of reach), holding a nail polish bottle and brush outside arm's reach to touch the lower legs and flip-flop-clad feet of a second person seated in front facing away from the wearer (~3–5 m away, medium-bright grey, resting on a white towel over the wearer's lap/stool above a blue foot basin). To the upper left (~3–5 m away, ~3–5 m to the left of the client's right leg), a third person's black-clad lower legs and sneakers extend into the frame from the left, while the upper bodies and heads of all three people remain out of view so it is impossible to see if anyone looks toward the wearer. Across frames 1 to 3 the scene is nearly static with the wearer's right hand slightly occluding the client's right foot, whereas in frames 4 and 5 the wearer leans forward and turns counterclockwise toward the left, making the client's legs advance toward the upper-right corner as the client lowers their left foot away from the blue basin (~3–5 m and out of reach) and the wearer's left knee enters the lower-left background (~3–5 m). The depth map clearly separates the vertical layering of the wearer's arms, the client's elevated calves and feet, the support cushion below them, and the recessed floor and basin in a way that is harder to gauge from the flat lighting of RGB alone. However, the depth map is unreliable around small details—merging the nail polish bottle, brush, and toe separators into the surrounding hands and feet—and in frame 5 it inaccurately renders the dark trousers of the wearer's left leg and the background floor as a single black void.
segmentation: The segmentation map attempts to partition the far-off workspace in front of the camera wearer (whose arms and lap sit at ~3–5 m and out of reach at the bottom) and the two other people partially visible in the scene: the client facing away from the wearer with bare lower legs extended from the top (~3–5 m away, ~3–5 m apart) and a third person's lower legs to the left (~3–5 m away), though everyone's upper bodies and faces are out of frame. Far outside the wearer's arm's reach (~3–5 m) are the client's feet in flip-flops with white toe separators, a white towel beneath them, a nail polish bottle and cap in the wearer's hands, and a blue basin far beyond the towel (~3–5 m and out of reach). Across frames 1 to 5, as the camera wearer extends their hands and rotates leftward in frames 4 and 5, the masks shift from a single large pink `person` region on the right to multiple fragmented masks as the client's left foot moves downward away from the basin and the wearer's left leg appears on the lower left. While frame 4 usefully isolates the client's two bare lower legs (light blue `person`) from the wearer's hands, towel, and left arm (pink and brown `person` masks) with sharp boundary contours, the segmentation map is largely unreliable throughout the sequence. It merges the white towel, cushion, and the wearer's arms into the client's `person` mask in frames 1–5, completely misses the third person's legs on the left in frames 2–5, and misclassifies the nail polish cap as a green `remote` in frame 3 and the blue stool edge as a purple `toilet` in frame 5.
pose: The pose map plots 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background for the camera wearer's hands (~3–5 m from the camera, out of reach, in the lower background) and, in frame 5, a false-positive yellow body skeleton near the client's left foot in the upper-right (~3–5 m away and out of reach), while providing no representation of the tiled floor, basin, towel, or the third person's legs ~3–5 m to the left. In frames 1 to 3, magenta hand skeletons appear at the bottom-right and bottom-center (~3–5 m apart) where the wearer's right hand holds a bottle and the left hand holds a brush outside arm's reach of the client's right foot just above them. In frame 4, as the wearer's left hand moves ~3–5 m leftward to hold the side of the client's right foot, only that left hand is tracked, and in frame 5 as the wearer turns leftward, only the wearer's right hand at the bottom-center is detected alongside the erroneous yellow torso/head keypoints superimposed on the client's advancing foot. When detected, the magenta finger joints explicitly show the articulated pinch and curl of the wearer's fingers even where the hands self-occlude or overlap the bottle and foot in RGB. However, the map is highly unreliable: it misses the wearer's left hand in frames 1 and 5 and right hand in frame 4, fails to detect any true leg or foot skeletons for the three partially visible people (whose heads and gaze directions are out of view), and hallucinates a tiny upper-body skeleton on the client's toes in frame 5.
